question_text: Why does a passenger fall forward when a moving bus suddenly stops? / चलती हुई बस (moving bus) के अचानक रुकने पर यात्री आगे की ओर क्यों गिरता है?
answer: Due to inertia of motion / गति के जड़त्व (inertia of motion) के कारण
options: Due to inertia of rest / विराम के जड़त्व (inertia of rest) के कारण
Due to inertia of motion / गति के जड़त्व (inertia of motion) के कारण
Due to gravitational force / गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल (gravitational force) के कारण
Due to friction / घर्षण (friction) के कारण
explanation: When the bus stops suddenly, the lower part of the passenger's body comes to rest with the bus, but the upper part continues to move forward due to the inertia of motion. / जब बस अचानक रुकती है, तो यात्री के शरीर का निचला हिस्सा बस के साथ रुक जाता है, लेकिन ऊपरी हिस्सा गति के जड़त्व के कारण आगे बढ़ता रहता है।
distractor_rationale: Inertia of rest applies when a stationary bus starts moving. Gravity pulls objects downwards, not forwards. Friction acts between the tires and the road to stop the bus, but it doesn't push the passenger forward.

ai_context.learning_goal: Understand how inertia of motion affects objects in moving vehicles.
common_misconceptions: Students often confuse inertia of rest with inertia of motion.
ai_context.hint: Think about what the upper body was doing before the bus stopped. Did it want to change its state?

question_text: If two teams pull a rope with a force of 100 N in opposite directions, what is the net force acting on the rope? / यदि दो टीमें एक रस्सी को विपरीत दिशाओं में 100 N के बल (force) से खींचती हैं, तो रस्सी पर कार्य करने वाला कुल बल क्या है?
options: 0 N
explanation: The forces are equal and opposite, so they cancel each other out. This is a balanced force, resulting in a net force of 0 N. / बल समान और विपरीत हैं, इसलिए वे एक-दूसरे को रद्द (cancel) कर देते हैं। यह एक संतुलित बल (balanced force) है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप कुल बल 0 N होता है।
distractor_rationale: 200 N would be if both pulled in the same direction. 100 N is the individual force, not the net force. 50 N is an arbitrary number.

ai_context.learning_goal: Calculate net force from balanced forces.
common_misconceptions: Students might add the forces together regardless of direction.
ai_context.hint: Forces are vectors. If one is +100 and the other is -100, what is the sum?

question_text: What force is needed to produce an acceleration of 2 m/s² in a body of mass 5 kg? / 5 kg द्रव्यमान (mass) वाले पिंड में 2 m/s² का त्वरण (acceleration) उत्पन्न करने के लिए कितने बल (force) की आवश्यकता होती है?
options: 7 N
explanation: According to Newton's Second Law, Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma). So, F = 5 kg × 2 m/s² = 10 N. / न्यूटन के दूसरे नियम के अनुसार, बल = द्रव्यमान × त्वरण (F = ma)। इसलिए, F = 5 kg × 2 m/s² = 10 N।
distractor_rationale: 2.5 N is mass divided by acceleration. 7 N is mass plus acceleration. 20 N is a calculation error.

ai_context.learning_goal: Apply the formula F = ma to calculate force.
common_misconceptions: Students might divide mass by acceleration instead of multiplying.
ai_context.hint: Use Newton's second law formula: Force equals mass times acceleration.

question_text: When a swimmer pushes the water backward, why does the swimmer move forward? / जब एक तैराक पानी को पीछे की ओर धकेलता है, तो वह आगे की ओर क्यों बढ़ता है?
answer: Because the water exerts an equal and opposite reaction force on the swimmer / क्योंकि पानी तैराक पर समान और विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया बल (reaction force) लगाता है
options: Because water has no inertia / क्योंकि पानी में कोई जड़त्व (inertia) नहीं होता
Because the water exerts an equal and opposite reaction force on the swimmer / क्योंकि पानी तैराक पर समान और विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया बल (reaction force) लगाता है
Because the swimmer's mass decreases / क्योंकि तैराक का द्रव्यमान (mass) कम हो जाता है
Because of the gravitational pull of the earth / पृथ्वी के गुरुत्वाकर्षण खिंचाव (gravitational pull) के कारण
explanation: According to Newton's Third Law of Motion, every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Pushing water back is the action, and the water pushing the swimmer forward is the reaction. / न्यूटन के गति के तीसरे नियम के अनुसार, प्रत्येक क्रिया की समान और विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया होती है। पानी को पीछे धकेलना क्रिया (action) है, और पानी द्वारा तैराक को आगे धकेलना प्रतिक्रिया (reaction) है।
distractor_rationale: Water has inertia. Mass does not decrease during swimming. Gravity pulls the swimmer downward, not forward.

ai_context.learning_goal: Identify action and reaction pairs in real-world scenarios.
common_misconceptions: Students might think action and reaction forces act on the same object, canceling each other out.
ai_context.hint: Think about Newton's third law. If you push something, what does it do to you?

question_text: Which object has more momentum: A 1000 kg car moving at 2 m/s, or a 10 kg bicycle moving at 20 m/s? / किस वस्तु में अधिक संवेग (momentum) है: 2 m/s की गति से चलने वाली 1000 kg की कार, या 20 m/s की गति से चलने वाली 10 kg की साइकिल?
options: The car / कार
The bicycle / साइकिल
Both have the same momentum / दोनों का संवेग (momentum) समान है
Cannot be determined / निर्धारित नहीं किया जा सकता
explanation: Momentum (p) = mass (m) × velocity (v). Car's momentum = 1000 kg × 2 m/s = 2000 kg·m/s. Bicycle's momentum = 10 kg × 20 m/s = 200 kg·m/s. The car has more momentum. / संवेग (p) = द्रव्यमान (m) × वेग (v)। कार का संवेग = 1000 kg × 2 m/s = 2000 kg·m/s। साइकिल का संवेग = 10 kg × 20 m/s = 200 kg·m/s। कार में अधिक संवेग है।
distractor_rationale: Students might think the faster object (bicycle) has more momentum without calculating. Or they might make a calculation error.

ai_context.learning_goal: Calculate and compare momentum for different objects.
common_misconceptions: Students often confuse velocity with momentum, thinking the faster object always has more momentum.
ai_context.hint: Momentum is calculated by multiplying mass and velocity (p = mv). Calculate it for both objects.
